data.question: Which supplied fictional tool is the better first trial for a solo creator making four videos monthly with an AUD 25 budget and a need for caption export?
data.scope: A comparison of advertised fit using exactly three provided snippets, without current-price verification or a purchase recommendation.
data.answer: QuillNest is the better first trial for this bounded comparison of advertised fit: its supplied AUD 19 monthly plan includes six projects, caption export, and one user, meeting the creator's four-video workload, AUD 25 budget, and solo workflow. [source-1][source-3] ClipHarbor also advertises caption export and one user, but its AUD 29 monthly price is AUD 4 over budget; its twenty-project allowance adds capacity the stated workload does not require. [source-2] Both cards advertise a seven-day trial, so the supplied trial duration does not favor either option. [source-1][source-2] These are fictional, unverified product claims, neither card establishes transcription accuracy, and the creator reports having tested neither tool. [source-1][source-2][source-3] The recommendation is therefore to trial QuillNest first, not to treat a paid purchase as justified. [source-1][source-2][source-3] Caption and export one representative video, checking correction time, unacceptable errors, and whether the export works in the intended editing workflow before deciding to pay.

findings.text: The supplied QuillNest card advertises AUD 19 per month, six projects, caption export, one user, and a seven-day trial.
The supplied ClipHarbor card advertises AUD 29 per month, twenty projects, caption export, one user, and a seven-day trial.
Against the user's AUD 25 budget and four-video workload, QuillNest's advertised plan fits; ClipHarbor costs AUD 4 over budget and offers capacity the stated workload does not require.
Neither card describes accuracy, and the creator's supplied note says neither tool has been tested.
QuillNest may be sufficient for the creator's actual caption workflow; one trial video could reveal unacceptable transcription errors or export friction.
